classification: C. After the quote normalises, the post-release window is statistically the same as a same-day control window: no direction, no excess volatility, nothing executable.
classification_text: The transition the brief describes exists and is measurable. The Dukascopy quote at 15:30:00 opens 2.3 times its normal width, peaks at 3.7 times inside the first second, and returns: below 2x normal after 5 seconds at the median, below 1.5x after 20 seconds, below 1.25x after 25 seconds, with a long tail (one event in four takes more than two minutes to reach 1.25x, one in ten more than four and a half minutes). Thursdays normalise more slowly than Fridays. The price, meanwhile, keeps moving: at the normalisation time only a quarter of the 30-minute displacement has happened, at 60 seconds a third, at 5 minutes two thirds. So the premise held: most of the post-release move happens with a normal spread.

The information did not. From the moment the spread has normalised, the probability of reaching +0.5 ATR before -0.5 ATR is 0.47 to 0.55 whichever way you look (either side, either weekday, 1 to 60 minutes), and the same for 1 ATR. Five shock states that could plausibly carry direction (displacement at normalisation, 5-second return, tick imbalance in the first 5 and next 25 seconds, which side of the quote moved) all give hit rates whose confidence intervals contain 0.5, and executable hit rates of 0.22 to 0.30. The first clean move continues 45 to 49 percent of the time and its mean 30-minute close is zero. Delayed momentum over 15 to 120 seconds with 30 to 60 minute holds is gross-positive by 0.4 to 0.7 ATR, but the identical rule at 16:30 and 17:15 on the same days is gross-positive by 0.5 ATR too, no cell reaches |t| = 2, and the pre-declared plateau rule retained nothing. That is 2025 gold drifting in the US session, not the release.

Track B fails the same way. From the normalisation time the market reaches 1 ATR in 138 seconds against 173 for the controls, and the 30-minute range is 3.5 ATR against 3.7: the release's extra volatility is spent inside the shock, where Phase 14 showed it cannot be bought. Every two-sided design placed after the shock (OCO breakouts at 0.25 to 0.75 ATR, the first-minute range breakout) is negative at one spread, worse at 1.25x, and within noise of the same rule at the control times. The pullback candidate was not built because its precondition failed. Outcome C, on development data only; 2026 was never read.
timeline: Two things stand out in the band table. First, the shock is a spread and displacement event, not a tick-count event: the tick rate is 5 to 10 per second in every band, including the first 100 milliseconds. Second, the tick direction is one-sided only while the quote is wide: the absolute tick imbalance is 1.0 in the first half second, 0.15 at 2 to 5 seconds and 0.07 from 10 seconds on, which is the level of a normal window. By the time a retail order could be placed with a normal spread, the order flow is already balanced.
normalisation: Normalisation is defined as the first time the rolling one-second median spread stays below the multiple of the pre-release normal (15:00 to 15:25 median, $0.57 or 0.21 ATR) for five seconds. A third of events are already below 2x at 15:30:00.000 because the widening arrives a few hundred milliseconds after the first tick; the max column of the band table shows it. Monday to Wednesday were not downloaded, so no curve exists for them; the brief's request for that split is recorded as not measurable with the data on disk. The economic calendar is unavailable, so Thursday and Friday are day-of-week groups, not event identities.
discovery: Read the sign-agreement column with care: the 73 percent agreement between the 60-second displacement and the 30-minute displacement is mostly the 60-second move being part of the 30-minute move. The clean test is the continuation table below, measured from the normalisation time in the direction of the move so far, and it is at or under 50 percent.
information: Executable hit rates at 0.25 ATR are 5 to 7 percent because at the 1.5x normalisation time the quote is still 0.31 ATR wide, so the losing side of a 0.25-ATR race is inside the spread at entry. That is the executability floor for this instrument: no target below about 0.3 ATR can be raced at all, and the mid-to-mid rows show that even without that floor the race is a coin flip.
states: The side-of-quote state (s_side: did the ask or the bid move more in the first 5 seconds) is the best-looking row at 0.58 on mid with a confidence interval of 0.46 to 0.69 and an executable rate of 0.30. Under the retention rule it is not a candidate, and it is one of five states tried, so its nominal value is inflated by selection.
continuation: Continuation and reversal are both inside the interval: the first clean move neither continues nor reverses with any reliability. The mean MFE and MAE over 30 minutes are symmetric (2.1 against 2.5 ATR) and the mean close is -0.01 ATR.
trackb: The only row where the event beats the control is time-to-move from 15:30:00 itself, which is the shock. From the normalisation time the event and the controls reach 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 ATR with the same frequency and at similar speed, and the 30-minute range is slightly smaller after the event than at 16:30 or 17:15.
oco: Mid-to-mid, the OCO breakout after normalisation makes 0.01 to 0.26 ATR per attempt; the two legs of spread cost about 0.3 ATR; net is -0.08 to -0.26. The delay-band matrix has two cells at +0.01 and +0.02 with standard errors of 0.10, surrounded by negative cells: no plateau. Controls with the same rules are -0.05 to -0.27. At 1.25x spread every cell is at or below -0.20.
momentum: The positive region (30 to 120 seconds, 30 to 60 minute holds) is real as a number and useless as a signal: the best cell is +0.45 ATR with t = 1.2, the same rule at the control times gives +0.30 with t = 1.3, and adding a 1-ATR stop removes most of it. The pre-declared rule (|t| >= 2 and both neighbouring delay bands positive) retained no cell. From the normalisation time itself the direction reverses on average by 0.3 ATR over 5 minutes, which is one spread: not executable and not pre-registered.
acceptance: Spread-normalisation curve reconstructed from ticks, per weekday
Direction after normalisation: hit rate above 0.55 with the interval excluding 0.5
Executable net positive with |t| >= 2 on development
Not met (event and control rows match within noise)
Track B: excess volatility after normalisation
controls: A: same-day 16:30 and 17:15 windows with every rule applied unchanged. B: mid-to-mid versus executable for every design (the cost scenario at 0). C: the Phase 14 random same-day straddle (-0.15 ATR) for the two-sided designs. D: weekday split for every table in the JSON. None separates the event from its controls.
next: Outcome C: the release hypothesis is closed at every level tried (bar-level straddle in Phase 13, tick straddle in Phase 14, post-shock transition here). Per section 20 of the brief, no further variants of it.

The one release-related source left is the calendar (surprise sign and size), which is a different hypothesis with a different data need; it stays DATA_INSUFFICIENT in the ledger until an event list with actual, forecast and timestamp exists.
The manual 100-trade log with skipped-signal records remains the highest-value unmeasured dataset.

An observation, not a candidate: the control rows show 2025 US-session continuation of about 0.5 ATR gross over 30 to 60 minutes without any release. Phase 12 already tested continuation families on 2021 to 2024 bars and rejected them after costs; if it is ever revisited it needs its own frozen spec on the bar dataset first, not on 2025 ticks.

Housekeeping: the tick downloader is in 2026 and stalls on holidays (Good Friday 2026 returns no data and burns retries); the 2026 files are for a later out-of-sample check only and have not been read. C: has 1.8 GB free; the eight busy MT5 symbol caches can be deleted after a terminal restart.
